entries.attack_pattern: cacheScope public poisoning with injected instructions
entries.description: A hostile MCP server returns a poisoned tools/list marked cacheScope public. The cached response contains malicious instructions or tool descriptions. Shared gateways re-serve the poisoned payload across authorization contexts, delivering prompt injection to every user.
indicators: cacheScope: public on tools/list
server-authored instructions in cached response
cross-user cache hits on discovery endpoints
entries.mitigation: Never cache discovery responses across identities. Treat instructions and tool descriptions as untrusted. Pin allowed servers.

entries.attack_pattern: poisoned tool schemas with malicious URLs
entries.description: A poisoned tools/list cached publicly may include tool schemas containing malicious URLs (webhook endpoints, documentation links, callback URLs). The URL screening applies to the payload, though the primary vector is the cache mechanism.
indicators: URLs in cached tool schemas
webhook URLs in poisoned tool definitions
entries.mitigation: Screen URLs in cached discovery responses. Validate webhook endpoints against allowlist.

entries.description: Cache poisoning techniques that do not match known tool-abuse patterns. The cross-context serving behavior (same discovery payload served to multiple authorization contexts) is itself a detectable synthetic anomaly.
indicators: identical discovery payload across user contexts
cacheScope public on user-specific data
entries.mitigation: Monitor for cross-context cache serving anomalies. Alert on cacheScope public for responses containing user-specific fields.

entries.attack_pattern: prompt injection via server instructions field
entries.description: MCP discovery responses include a server-controlled instructions field that clients fold into the system prompt with no sanitization, validation, or length limit. This is direct prompt injection via the discovery protocol.
indicators: instructions field in initialize or tools/list response
instruction text in system prompt context
unbounded instruction length
entries.mitigation: Bound instruction length. Isolate server instructions from trusted system prompt. Sanitize before folding into context.

entries.description: Injected instructions via the instructions field frequently aim at data exfiltration (export database URL, send conversation history, reveal API keys). The pii_leak category catches the exfiltration consequence of a successful 015 injection.
indicators: instructions containing exfiltration verbs
PII in tool call arguments following instruction injection
entries.mitigation: Monitor tool calls for PII exfiltration patterns following discovery. Block exfiltration instructions at the proxy.

entries.description: Novel techniques for abusing the instructions field (multi-turn setup, encoded instructions, instruction chaining across tools, steganographic instructions) that evade known prompt injection signatures.
indicators: encoded content in instructions field
multi-tool instruction chaining
instructions referencing other tools
entries.mitigation: Apply anomaly detection to instructions field content. Flag unusually long or encoded instructions.

entries.attack_pattern: cross-tenant system prompt injection via chained cache poisoning
entries.description: A single poisoned discovery response (015 injection payload) marked cacheScope public (008 amplifier) delivers prompt injection to every user behind a shared gateway. One poisoned response becomes cross-tenant system-prompt injection.
indicators: cacheScope public + instructions field in same response
identical injected instructions across tenant contexts
entries.mitigation: The proxy must screen discovery responses before caching. Never cache instructions fields across identities.

entries.description: The cross-tenant serving pattern (single server instructions appearing across multiple user contexts via shared cache) is a detectable synthetic anomaly independent of the payload content.
indicators: server instructions in multiple tenant contexts
cache hit rate anomaly on discovery endpoints
entries.mitigation: Detect cross-tenant instruction propagation. Alert when discovery payloads cross authorization boundaries.

entries.attack_pattern: amplified data exfiltration via cross-tenant injection
entries.description: Cross-tenant prompt injection multiplies the blast radius of any data exfiltration instruction. A single exfiltration instruction in a poisoned cached response targets every user's data.
indicators: exfiltration instructions in cached discovery
PII exfiltration across multiple tenants from single source
entries.mitigation: Block exfiltration patterns in discovery responses before caching. Isolate tenant data flows.

excluded_thin_fits.reason: Cache poisoning is a delivery mechanism, not a kit signature
Only in misconfiguration variant, not core attack
No kit evidence for instructions-field vector (UNKNOWN)
